title: crumbkit/self-environment-list/v1
description: The environment variables that the tool declares and the library reads, each with its rules and the value it has in this process.

cut.description: Present when the output budget cut the result short, so data holds only its first rows.

budget.description: The most bytes that the run printed on standard output.

data.description: The rows of the page, up to the limit.

dry_run.description: Present, and true, when the run was a dry run that changed nothing.

next.description: The next steps, in the order the text prints them. It is absent when there are none.

commands.description: The commands that carry out the step, in order.

call.description: A command line of this tool.

run.description: A command line of another program.

text.description: The sentence or phrase that the text prints for the step.

total.description: The number of rows that matched, of which data holds one page. It is absent when the tool did not count the rows.

truncated.description: True when the document leaves out rows that matched, because of the limit or the output budget, and false when data holds every row.

Described.description: One value of a named enumeration with its description.

description.description: The sentence that says what choosing the value means.

Listed.description:
One variable of `self environment list`: the fields of
[`Explained`] and the library that owns the variable.

bind.description: The variable's bind, such as a 1Password reference, when it has one.

cache.description: `never` when the bind keeps the value out of any cache of resolved values; empty, and left out of `--json`, when a cache may keep it.

check.description: The sentence that states the check the application's own code makes of the value, which starmap never runs; empty, and left out of `--json`, when the spec states none.

effect.description: The sentence that says what the application does when the variable is unset; empty, and left out of `--json`, when the spec states none.

enumeration.description: The name of the named enumeration that the variable's type is; left out of `--json` for any other type.

group.description: The name of the group of variables that are set together or not at all, which the variable belongs to; empty, and left out of `--json`, when it belongs to none.

owner.description: The library that reads the variable in every tool, such as `crumbkit`; empty, and left out of `--json`, for a variable that the tool's own declaration holds.

purpose.description: The sentence that says what the variable is for.

show.description: Whether the value may be shown or is withheld.

source.description: Where the variable's value comes from, with the kind of its bind.

state.description: Where the value comes from: `set` when this shell sets the variable, `default` when it leaves the variable unset and the default applies, `unset` when the variable has no value, and `invalid` when this shell sets a value that does not fit the type. The same state as `value.state`, at the top level.

type.description: The type of the variable's value, such as port or integer 1..=100.

unset.description: What happens when the variable has no value, in local mode and, when it differs, in production.

value.description: The variable's value in this shell, or its default; a withheld value prints as eight dots and has no text in JSON.

state.description:
Whether the value comes from this shell, is the default, is unset,
or comes from this shell and does not fit the variable's type.

text.description: The value's text. A withheld value never has one.

values.description: Each value of a named enumeration with its description; empty, and left out of `--json`, for any other type.

State.description: Where a variable's value comes from in this shell.

oneOf.description: This shell leaves the variable unset, and its default applies.
This shell sets the variable to a value that does not fit its type.
